gaps.sentence: This month they ___ a new wing to the hospital, so some services are elsewhere.
gaps.hint: this month means a temporary current period
gaps.explanation: 'This month' describes a temporary situation around now, so the present continuous fits: are adding.

gaps.sentence: Don't disturb him — he ___ an important video call with the client.
gaps.hint: do not disturb means it is happening now
gaps.explanation: An action in progress at the moment of speaking takes the present continuous: is having.

gaps.sentence: I ___ coffee at all, but I drink tea every morning.
gaps.hint: a general habit contrasted with another habit
gaps.explanation: A permanent habit takes the present simple, so the negative form is: don't drink.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her laptop repaired twice this year already.
gaps.explanation: 'Has had it repaired twice this year' — present perfect of causative have.

gaps.sentence: Water ___ at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
gaps.hint: a timeless scientific fact takes present simple
gaps.explanation: General truths and scientific facts take the present simple: boils.

gaps.hint: on the point of happening now
gaps.explanation: 'Be about to' expresses something on the point of happening: is about to start.

gaps.sentence: While I ___ the report yesterday, my laptop battery died.
gaps.hint: the battery died interrupted the writing
gaps.explanation: The dying battery interrupted the ongoing writing, so the past continuous fits: was writing.

gaps.sentence: This jacket ___ to my brother, so please do not take it by mistake.
gaps.hint: belong is always a state verb
gaps.explanation: 'Belong' is a state verb and has no continuous form, so the present simple is correct: belongs.
